topic: Pi Coding Agent Config Folder Out of Place on Linux: Fix and Workflow
research_method: GitHub REST API via authenticated gh CLI (exact issue/PR metadata, comments, source code, raw docs), HN Algolia API (thread text), raw.githubusercontent.com docs, targeted web search. No browser rendering used.
summary: Pi (the terminal coding agent at earendil-works/pi, formerly badlogic/pi-mono) keeps ALL of its per-user state in a home-root dotdir: the agent directory defaults to ~/.pi/agent, and the default session directory is a CHILD of it (~/.pi/agent/sessions via getSessionsDir()). That is why Linux users file 'config folder is out of place' bugs. The maintainer has explicitly and repeatedly refused XDG compliance: PR #256 (XDG + auto-migration) was closed unmerged in Dec 2025, issue #534 was closed the same day it was opened in Jan 2026, #2870 was closed as 'just ridiculous', #3310 (split state from config) and #5301 (opt-in XDG behind a Paths object) were both refused, and #7274 was auto-closed. The escape hatch is the env var PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR (plus PI_CODING_AGENT_SESSION_DIR, added later to split sessions out). The single most important gotcha: PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR is used VERBATIM as the agent directory - no '/agent' is appended - so pointing it at ~/.config/pi while your files sit in ~/.config/pi/agent silently yields 'no auth, no models'. PI_CONFIG_DIR looks like the fix and does nothing in the coding agent (0 code references; it belonged to the removed 'pods' tool). This article is the missing how-to: exact recipe, migration steps, verification, and the version-control / read-only-home workflows that motivated the whole debate.
verification_notes: Repo metadata (stars/forks/open issues/licence/latest release) read live from the GitHub API on 2026-10-01, authenticated as gh CLI user baeseokjae; both github.com/badlogic/pi-mono and github.com/earendil-works/pi resolve to the same repo record (full_name = earendil-works/pi), so pi-mono is a legacy redirect, not a second repo.

Every maintainer quote is the literal body of a GitHub issue/PR comment fetched via /repos/earendil-works/pi/issues/{n}/comments - not a paraphrase. Issue numbers, states, open/close timestamps and comment counts are from the API.

The getAgentDir()/getSessionsDir() behaviour and the ENV_AGENT_DIR/ENV_SESSION_DIR constants were read from packages/coding-agent/src/config.ts on main (raw.githubusercontent.com), not inferred from docs.

'PI_CONFIG_DIR has no effect' was verified two ways: a GitHub code search for PI_CONFIG_DIR in the repo returned total_count 0, and maintainer comment on issue #2390 states it is for pods, not the coding agent.
Pi is NOT installed on this host (no pi binary, no ~/.pi), so the recipe is written from source + documented behaviour and was not executed here. Do not claim hands-on verification of the commands.
Star count (110,843) and the v0.99.2 release date (2026-09-30T19:30:47Z) are point-in-time and will drift.

key_points: The canonical thread and the URL that ranks for this query; opened 2026-01-07 by Ramblurr and closed by the maintainer the same day (16 comments).
Proposed rule: check PI_CONFIG_DIR, then XDG_CONFIG_HOME, else OS default (Linux/BSD $HOME/.config), then <prefix>/pi.
Maintainer: 'Yeah, I regret not doing this from the beginning... migrating this automatically for them is super icky, I'm afraid we'll have to live with it. The PI_CONFIG_DIR is your escape hook.'
Ramblurr's backwards-compatible proposal (use legacy layout if $HOME/.pi exists, else XDG, no migration) was never accepted; a PR offer went unanswered.
Community workarounds in-thread: PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR, symlink ~/.config/pi -> ~/.pi, or per-file symlinks; users report PI_CONFIG_DIR 'didn't seem to do anything'.
Thread was revived on HN in Aug 2026 and is still accumulating comments (last update 2026-08-18).
The only dedicated blog post on the topic (2026-06-17); explains the asymmetry that breaks most people's first attempt.
Default (no env var): agent dir is ~/.pi/agent, so auth.json/models.json live in ~/.pi/agent/.
Override: PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR is used verbatim as the agent dir - no /agent is appended.
Shows the wrong form (PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR=~/.piz -> reads ~/.piz/auth.json, empty) and the fix (PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR=~/.piz/agent).
Quotes getAgentDir() from config.ts and frames ~/.pi as a container that can hold several independent agent dirs (agent, work, personal).
No migration steps, no session-dir split, no dotfiles workflow - the gaps this article can fill.
The XDG-compliance request (2026-04-06, 22 comments, labelled bug, closed same day); asks to split config -> ~/.config/pi/agent, state -> ~/.local/state/pi/agent, cache -> ~/.cache/pi/agent.
Maintainer response is the most quotable refusal: 'nope, definitely not going full gpt like this' and 'that's just ridiculous. things will stay as is.'

Sustained counter-argument in-thread: opencode demonstrably follows XDG (/home/mks/.{config,local/share,local/state,cache}/opencode); enduity notes opencode is not squeaky clean either (it drops a .gitignore in ~/.config/opencode).
Real user pain, not aesthetics: dotfiles repos, readonly $HOME, state on a different partition, deciding what is safe to rm -rf.
Later comments (Sep 2026) still ask whether the decision will ever be revisited; the thread remains the reference for 'it will not change'.

The most constructive proposal (2026-06-01): centralise path policy behind a Paths/Roots object with a .pi implementation and an XDG implementation, chosen by whether ~/.pi exists - no automated migration, new users get XDG.
Closed within 13 minutes by the new-contributor auto-close bot, then explicitly refused by the maintainer: 'sorry, this isn't going to change for the time being.'
Author notes the alternatives that DO exist (PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR, PI_CODING_AGENT_SESSION_DIR) but argues config-vs-state hygiene should be right out of the box.
Best-documented technical explanation of why a fork/patch must touch path resolution in many managers, not one function - useful context for readers tempted to fork.
Official documentation: 'User-level configuration lives in the agent directory, which defaults to ~/.pi/agent'; set it with PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR or the SDK's agentDir option.
Full inventory of what lives in <agent-dir>: settings.json, keybindings.json, mcp.json, models.json, auth.json, AGENTS.md/SYSTEM.md/APPEND_SYSTEM.md, extensions/, skills/, prompts/, themes/.

Separate project-level .pi/ directory in the working tree (settings.json, mcp.json, extensions/, skills/, prompts/, themes/) loaded after project trust - so 'out of place' applies to both $HOME/.pi and <repo>/.pi.
Documents the sessionDir setting and that PI_CODING_AGENT_SESSION_DIR / --session-dir override it; environment-variables.md lists both vars with their defaults.
Notably silent on XDG: no Linux-specific guidance, no migration, which is exactly why the recipe must be assembled from source and threads.

A Nix packager already works around it in a wrapper: 'export PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR=${PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR:-$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/pi}' with PI_OFFLINE/PI_SKIP_VERSION_CHECK set by default

Third-party package pi-profiles exists precisely because PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR relocates auth: its launcher sets PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR per profile and restores shared sessions by setting PI_CODING_AGENT_SESSION_DIR to Pi's standard ~/.pi/agent/sessions
OpenCode (the commonly cited XDG-compliant alternative) keeps four separate roots: ~/.config/opencode, ~/.local/share/opencode, ~/.local/state/opencode, ~/.cache/opencode

angles: Recipe-first: the article is the missing how-to. Every existing source is either a refusal thread or a one-gotcha blog post - nobody writes the actual migration + verification steps.
The verbatim trap as the hook: 'PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR is used as-is, the default appends /agent' explains the #1 silent failure (no auth, no models) and is quotable from source.
The asymmetry nobody documents: config has its own var, but SESSIONS default to a child of the config dir - so moving config drags session state along unless you also set PI_CODING_AGENT_SESSION_DIR.
Dead end warning: PI_CONFIG_DIR looks like the fix, is mentioned in the maintainer's own comment, and does nothing in the coding agent (0 code refs). Readers lose hours here.

Timeline as authority: 5 refusals across 10 months (PR #256, #534, #3310, #2870, #5301, #7274) with literal quotes - 'this isn't going to change for the time being'. Justifies 'stop waiting for upstream, do this instead'.
Honest counterweight: not everyone wants XDG; some users like one self-contained dotdir, and Pi's own threads contain both camps. Present the trade-off instead of a strawman.

Workflow section that competitors skip: dotfiles/version-control recipe (what to commit, what to gitignore), read-only $HOME setups, multi-profile agent dirs, Nix wrapper, and the pi-profiles launcher.
Verification section: how to prove Pi is reading the new location (env propagation to the shell tool, PI_SESSION_FILE, settings/agent-dir visibility) rather than assuming the move worked.

faq.q: Does Pi follow the XDG Base Directory Specification?
faq.a: No. The agent directory defaults to ~/.pi/agent and project config defaults to <repo>/.pi. XDG support has been requested and refused repeatedly (PR #256, issues #534, #2870, #3310, #5301, #7274). The maintainer's position: 'this isn't going to change for the time being.'

faq.q: What is the correct value for PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR?
faq.a: Whatever directory should BE the agent directory. It is used verbatim - no /agent is appended. If you want the equivalent of the default layout at an XDG location, use PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR="$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/pi/agent". Setting it to "$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/pi" while the files are in .../pi/agent is the classic silent failure.

faq.q: Can I move just the sessions and leave the config in ~/.pi?
faq.a: Yes - set PI_CODING_AGENT_SESSION_DIR (or the sessionDir setting, or --session-dir). Precedence: --session-dir beats PI_CODING_AGENT_SESSION_DIR beats the sessionDir setting. This is the practical way to keep ~/.local/state free to be wiped.
No. It belonged to the removed 'pods' tool; the maintainer says so explicitly and the variable has zero references in the pi codebase. Use PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR.

faq.q: Will Pi migrate my old config automatically?
faq.a: No. Migration was part of the rejected PR #256. Move the files yourself (or symlink) and keep the old directory absent so nothing writes to both.
